identification: Recovered AutoIt Yuner.A / WORM_AUTORUN.BWK worm source
reason: Destructive multi-vendor antivirus targeting, randomized hidden resident copies, renewed login persistence, document executable lures and removable autorun propagation code contradict any ordinary administration purpose.
provenance_limits: Only source was supplied. No containing registry package, binary, registry state, installer, consent or deployment context was supplied. Treat this as malicious program code, not proof it ran or infected the collection host.

external_identity_comparison.role: Identity comparison after independent reverse engineering; not a scan or hash conviction.
correspondence: CLV.Classes Com1-Com4 and StartCom1-StartCom2 registry data
Specific antivirus installation targets and removable autorun

execution_trace.effect: Array helpers and a two-round password-dependent byte-XOR/RC4-like cipher protect six randomly generated executable/startup names in HKLM\Software\Classes\CLV.Classes. The PRGA omits RC4 state swaps, so do not label it standard RC4. There is no embedded ciphertext to decode; encrypted values are created at runtime or supplied by registry state.

Select branches detect Kaspersky/AVG/Avira/Avast. AVG and Avira/Avast paths close processes and recursively delete vendor directories, then try to rename/hide survivors. Kaspersky branch manipulates its UI and strips AVP autostart. Kaspersky/AVG cases install Once.exe through the Windows load value, show fabricated error dialogs and log off.

If the running basename is none of the four generated names, copy @AutoItExe to the system directory four times, append varying bytes, mark hidden/system/read-only/archive, launch each name and show the original document or a generated RTF decoy before exit.

V1 disables registry and command tools, changes Explorer visibility, disables security notifications and System Restore, deletes SafeBoot configuration, changes hostname and script associations, renames VB runtime DLLs, starts V3 and enters GETDRIVES.
V4 and V2 run window-killing loops. UNTERMINATEME respawns missing peers through hidden cmd.exe /c calls. V2 repeatedly removes AVP autostart and writes worm Run values, with S4 uninitialized.

V3 recursively traverses fixed drives. For .doc files, CHANGEATTRIB creates <document>.doc.exe from V1, appends noise, renames the original document to .nal and hides it. Opening a lure temporarily restores and displays the original document.
GETDRIVES intends periodic removable-drive self-copy and .inf autorun repair, invoking a removable document scan. COPYAUTO writes open, shellexecute and Explorer/Open command entries.
CHANGEMD5 appends random-number/timer text to copies. It changes file hashes; it does not calculate an MD5 digest.

limitations: The supplied .au3 is source, not a PE. @AutoItExe is the compiled program only in compiled deployment; interpreted invocation copies the AutoIt runtime and does not establish successful self-replication.
GETDRIVES passes the whole DVAR array to DriveSpaceTotal and compares it with A: rather than using DVAR[I]; this can prevent or abort USB propagation.
S4 is declared but never initialized, so the third Run value may be unnamed rather than the intended randomized name.
Directory delete-then-move operations may fail after successful deletion; protected HKLM/system-directory writes depend on access rights, with no elevation mechanism in this script.
Broad WinKill title fragments can kill unrelated applications; no network/C2, credential theft or victim-file encryption path is present in this supplied source.

The new destruction-with-document-lures composite belongs to impact/degrade/edr/teardown. Crypto operations retain direction under crypto/encrypt and crypto/decrypt; helper names do not establish RC4.
